name: Advantage from the natural environment
idea: The work argues that a firm's relationship with the natural environment can be a source of lasting competitive advantage. It names linked capabilities, such as preventing pollution and taking responsibility for products across their life, and extends the resource-based view of the firm to cover them.
suggests: Look at which environmental capabilities the company has built, and whether they are hard for competitors to copy or only a cost of doing business.
limits: The work builds on the resource-based view of the firm, so what it argues rests on that view's way of explaining advantage.
competing_idea: The work starts from the point that earlier accounts of competitive advantage left the natural environment out, and it offers its view as a way to bring it in.
questions: Which environmental capabilities does the company have, and how did it build them?
Would competitors find these capabilities hard to copy, or could they match them quickly?
Does a planned environmental investment add to the company's advantage, or does it only meet a rule?

originals.reference: Stuart L. Hart, "A Natural-Resource-Based View of the Firm", Academy of Management Review, Vol. 20 No. 4, October 1995, pp. 986-1014
